newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends mixed, nearbys slip on ACPC news.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends mixed, nearbys slip on ACPC news.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mixed on Friday, with the nearbys pulling back amid news that more arabica coffee would be finding its way to the market, dealers said.

Most-active May fell 3.40 cents a lb on the day, to 165.75 cents, after ranging between 171.20 and 165.50. Second-month July finished 1.65 lower, at 155.55, while the back months closed down 0.80 to up 2.05.

Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) agreed at a technical meeting Thursday to release an additional 200,000 bags of washed arabica coffee and revoke an earlier export quota of 300,000 bags for the first half of 1997 to help satisfy roaster demand.
"There was a commission house sell-off on the ACPC news," one trader said. "There's more coffee coming and that knocked the weak longs out."
While some market participants said the export increase would ease supply concerns, others claimed the supply crunch was likely to resurface in the second half of the year.

The ACPC, which is expected to ratify Thursday's decision at a full council meeting in May, has also asked members to submit by April 15 proposals on coffee market stabilization plans. The current one-year export quota program is due to run out by the end of June.
Traders are keeping an eye on Colombia, where a truck drivers union is due to meet on Saturday to set the date for a nationwide strike.
On the charts, May near-term support was seen at today's low of 165.50 cents, a double bottom on the charts. Resistance was pegged at 172.00 cents, traders said.
Turnover was estimated at 8,624 lots, traders said.
